2020-9.cat: advanced practice registered nurses in autonomous practice
2020-9.q: APRNs who pay physicians for supervision will achieve cost-savings if they qualify for and register to practice autonomously since supervision will no longer be needed.
2020-9.note: practitioners counted as a kind of business, as in ../flhouse/bills/judge.json (dentists, physicians)

2020-30.note: grant match requirement lowered; no kind of business named as benefiting

2020-38.cat: substance use treatment providers and recovery residences
2020-38.q: According to the DCF, substance use treatment providers and recovery residences may realize savings by being able to fill positions faster with the changes identified in the bill.

2020-41.cat: residential recycling collectors and recovered materials processing facilities
2020-41.q: The bill may have a positive fiscal impact on the private sector because residential recycling collectors are not required to collect or transport contaminated recyclable materials and recovered materials processing facilities are not required to process contaminated recyclable materials

2020-56.cat: owners and operators of petroleum-contaminated sites in state cleanup programs
2020-56.q: The bill will have a positive fiscal impact on participants in the Advanced Cleanup Program, as the bill requires the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) to pay for the limited contamination assessment.
2020-56.note: judgment call: program participants are owners/operators of petroleum storage sites

2020-60.cat: intermediate care facilities for the developmentally disabled
2020-60.q: CS/SB 1344 may have a positive but indeterminate fiscal impact on ICFDD applicants that obtain the newly created CON exemption.

2020-70.q: This may attract trust business to Florida and prevent existing grantor trusts from fleeing to states perceived to be more trust-friendly.
2020-70.note: judgment call: "trust business" read as the trust industry

2020-78.q: Physicians exempted under CS/SB 1742 may see a positive fiscal impact due to no longer having to pay licensure and inspection fees

2020-87.cat: ride-hailing (TNC) drivers and limousine and for-hire vehicle operators
2020-87.q: The bill authorizes the use of TNC digital advertising devices, thus enabling TNC drivers to install the devices and earn additional monthly revenue. The bill also authorizes certain limousine and for-hire vehicle owners and drivers to begin operating as or with a luxury ground TNC

2020-95.note: analysis names families, not private schools, as beneficiaries

2020-105.cat: aerospace businesses financed by Space Florida
2020-105.q: The bill may result in a positive direct economic impact for businesses that are involved in activities financed by Space Florida.

2020-108.q: Motor vehicle dealers may experience a reduction in insurance premiums and the cost of litigation.

2020-109.cat: makers and sellers of automatic vote tabulating machines
2020-109.q: The bill may result in a positive fiscal impact to private sector companies that manufacture or sell automatic tabulating machines.

2020-124.q: Pharmacies that choose to employ automated pharmacy systems will incur costs associated with obtaining and maintaining those systems, but may increase revenue.

2020-126.cat: RV park owners and RV dealers/installers
2020-126.q: The bill allows RV parks to more easily eject unwanted guests, which may result in a positive fiscal impact to park owners who can rent spaces to other guests

2020-127.cat: CCNA professional services, construction management and project management firms
2020-127.q: The bill may have a positive, yet indeterminate fiscal impact on private sector businesses that provide professional services as defined in the CCNA, or that provide construction management or project management services

2020-145.cat: vendors of school panic alert systems
2020-145.q: Panic alert systems for a public school would be sold by private sector vendors, and would therefore have a positive impact on vendors selling a panic alert system.

2020-156.cat: multiphasic health testing centers, portable x-ray providers and other clinics exempted from licensure
2020-156.q: multiphasic health testing centers will no longer be required to pay the biennial license renewal fee of $952.64. The bill exempts from health care clinic licensure, community mental health partial-hospitalization programs, and portable x-ray providers, and rural health care clinics. These providers will no longer be required to pay the $2,000 biennial license renewal fee.

2020-160.note: fee reductions for licensees across many professions; no kind of business named as benefiting (same rule as ../flhouse judge 2023-68)
